Second ferry for the estuary?

By a staff reporter · 12 March

Larkspur Ferries has asked for public money to buy a second vessel, so that a breakdown no longer stops the only crossing between the harbour and Eastpoint.

What the operator says

The operator says the crossing saves commuters a forty minute drive, and that demand has grown every summer since the service began.

  • Two vessels would allow a winter timetable.
  • A third hull is mentioned “for later”.

What the assessors will ask

Assessors are expected to question the passenger forecast, which rests on a single summer survey, and the terminal lease, which ends before the loan does.

Related

Pier repairs delayed again

What happens next

A decision is due in the autumn. The operator will publish a revised cost table first.
